title: Tactile UI Pull-Cord Bulb - Detent & Snap Toggle Component

affordance_translation.physical_behavior: A pull-cord switch: the cord resists as you pull, the internal detent trips with a snap, force drops, and the filament warms from dull red to white while the lamp sways on its cord.
affordance_translation.digital_mechanic: A shadcn-style component engineered for the full force curve: an under-detent pull visibly lags the pointer, at the trip point force drops and the acorn catch-up reads as the snap; a pull that never reaches the trip point stretches the cord, tilts the lamp and springs back without switching. Filament color temperature (2200-3200K option) animates with state; light direction option (0-345 degrees) drives every highlight and shadow consistently.

design_tokens.borders: Spun-dome shade silhouette; acorn pull knob as the sole decorative element
design_tokens.elevation: Light-direction-aware highlight/shadow system that follows one configurable light angle
design_tokens.typography: Component-label minimal; state announced to assistive tech, not drawn

interactive_mechanics: Pointer-lag under detent, force-drop snap at trip point, spring-back on incomplete pulls
Filament warmth animation tied to on/off state
Optional synthesized snap sound, gated to start only after first user touch (autoplay-safe)
Page-finish integration: pull sets data-finish (aluminium/graphite) and persists the choice
usability_notes: The most complete published spec for cord-physics as UI: explicit lag/snap/spring-back states distinguish 'tried but not enough' from 'done' - a crucial but rarely modeled affordance. Ships as an installable component with aria label, keyboard pull(), and reduced-motion-friendly design. Use as the reference implementation when the pull-cord metaphor needs to be real UI, not illustration. Source: tactileui.dev component documentation.
